State model: MCP is stateless per-user; no server-side session state. Resources exist per workspace: overview, artifact inventory, findings, receipts summary, context packs; tokens authorize read-only MCP surface; tools include search_index, get_artifact, log_progress, request_context_pack, get_findings, record_note. Access events are fire-and-forget and do not mutate MCP state; no commit of code via MCP; no repository mutation through MCP.

Forbidden capabilities (as per guardrails and ADRs):
- No repo mutations or write operations via MCP (no write to repository; advisory PR only path remains outside MCP tool surface).
- No ownership-leaking cross-tenant data via MCP responses; tenant isolation on all reads.
- No Sampling/Roots/Logging or protocol sessions allowed by MCP (stateless core). 
- No persistent storage of raw repository contents; only transient fetches with minimal persisted metadata; no raw source or tokens stored in MCP surfaces.
- No direct/autonomous code execution or code mutation by MCP tools; no driving actions that mutate the repo from MCP.
- No in-tree doc bodies inline into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md via MCP surfaces; all such content must be controlled via managed markers and not embedded in surfaces.
- No charges or credits for failed or schema-invalid AI outputs; idempotent handling only; no double-charging via MCP surface.
- No usage of deprecated MCP features (sampling/roots/logging or protocol sessions).
- No export/import or cross-munge of contexts beyond MCP-provided context packs per task; no leakage of prompts in access logs; no sensitive artifacts in MCP responses.

Summary: The hosted MCP is stateless, token-based, streamable HTTP, designed to serve per-user context packs and findings without mutating repos, with strict tenant isolation and no raw code persistence or protocol sessions.

The protocol is Streamable HTTP with tenant isolation, no protocol sessions, and no Sampling/Roots/Logging per ADR.
Contract: per-user scoped tokens; on-demand context packs; read-only surface for most interactions; advisory PR flow as data mutation path.

Hosted MCP state model: per-user scoped tokens; resources: overview, artifacts, findings, receipts, context packs; on-demand serving; access events logged to a realtime channel; no server-side sessions; ttl-based caching; read operations idempotent.

Forbidden capabilities: no MPC writes to repo outside advisory PR; no repository mutations; no raw code bodies persist; no inlining of document bodies into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md; no storage of prompt/task texts; no protocol sessions; no Sampling/Roots/Logging; no cross-tenant data leakage; no charges for failed/schema-invalid outputs; no public marketplace; no bots performing autonomous repo changes; no data exports beyond defined MCP surfaces.

findings: Identified MCP protocol state model as stateless, per-user tokens, with advisory PR mutation path only.
Enforced prohibition on repo mutations; writes allowed only via advisory PR proposals (contents:read + pull_requests:write optional).
Prohibited capabilities explicitly include Sampling/Roots/Logging and protocol sessions, aligned with ADR-003 and ADR-002 guidance.
